implementation_notes: scala.concurrent is where the fan-out starts: Future.traverse(parts)(route) sequences one future per part and completes when all of them complete (failing fast on the first failure), and the aggregation is a foldLeft over the resulting List - the list order is the correlation state. All of it runs on an ExecutionContext, and the documentation stresses that blocking inside futures can starve the pool, so name a dedicated ExecutionContext for blocking part handlers instead of using the global one.
pitfalls: traverse fails fast on the first failed Future but does not cancel the others; partial aggregates need recovered futures or transformWith.
Blocking part handlers on ExecutionContext.global starve the ForkJoinPool - the futures overview recommends a dedicated ExecutionContext for long-lasting blocking work.
Futures are eager: traverse starts every part immediately, so a large composite needs batching to respect downstream limits.

variants.name: Akka Streams mapAsync + runFold (streaming parts)
variants.implementation_notes: In Akka Streams the composite is a materialized graph: Source(parts).mapAsync(n)(route) runs up to n parts concurrently and preserves the input order (mapAsyncUnordered drops it), stream back-pressure replaces a hand-rolled concurrency limit, and runFold performs the aggregation when the source completes - the operator page states that up to n elements are processed concurrently while 'regardless of their completion time the incoming order will be kept'. Choose it when parts stream from a broker and the aggregate must be computed under back-pressure.
variants.code_sketch:
Source(split(order))
  .mapAsync(4)(part => route(part))              // ordered, bounded fan-out
  .runFold(Report.empty)((acc, r) => acc.merge(r))
  .andThen { case Success(report) => emit(report) }
pitfalls: A failed inner Future fails the whole stream unless a supervision strategy or recover/recoverWith sits at the right stage.
mapAsync preserves input order and therefore lets a slow first part hold up later results; use mapAsyncUnordered when the aggregate is order-independent.
runFold only emits after the source completes: a source that stays open (a broker subscription) never produces the aggregate - use a bounded source or a timeout stage.
